text:
maria: Customer 4321 opened a support ticket — they rotated an API key 45m ago, we see the Vault revoke event, but the app still accepts the old key via the edge proxy. Customer is hitting 200s for some requests and 403s for others. Repro below and logs attached.

maria: repro curl (redacted keys):
```
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer OLD_KEY_REDACTED' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# sometimes 200, sometimes 403
```

maria: from proxy logs (redacted):
```
[2026-03-16T18:12:03Z] proxy auth: allowlist hit customer=4321 key=<redacted>
[2026-03-16T18:12:03Z] vault: revoke event key_id=sk_live_abc123 ttl=0
[2026-03-16T18:12:03Z] proxy: forwarded request -> backend
[2026-03-16T18:12:04Z] backend auth: key not found -> 403
```

jon: interesting — looks like proxy has an allowlist cache and it forwards without re-checking Vault. can you paste the ticket id and an example request-id from headers so I can correlate?

maria: ticket #T-8971, example request-id header: rq_20260316_9f3b

alex: quick hypothesis: proxy consults an in-memory allowlist with a TTL of 10m; when key is revoked in Vault we don't push invalidation to the edge cluster. sometimes the backend validates and returns 403, other times proxy bypasses backend auth and returns 200. :thinking_face:

vault-bot: Vault event: key_id=sk_live_abc123 was revoked by user=maria at 2026-03-16T17:27:01Z (event id vault_ev_98765)

ingrid: ok. safest immediate mitigation is to invalidate the proxy allowlist for customer 4321 and force proxy to do live Vault checks for that customer until we patch. Can infra run:
```
redis-cli -h edge-redis-prod --eval scripts/del_allowlist.lua 4321
# or directly: HDEL allowlist:customer:4321 <key-hash>
```

jon: I can run that. Quick check: do we have a rolling restart requirement? If in-memory only, HDEL should be sufficient; if nodes keep copies we may need to broadcast a cache invalidation message. I'll coordinate with infra.

alex: long term fix: proxy should check revocation metadata from Vault on allowlist hit or subscribe to Vault revocation webhook and evict automatically. For now minimal change: add a lightweight expiry check (fetch metadata TTL) before trusting allowlist entries for high-risk customers.

maria: customer is asking for timeline and whether keys are safe. Also they noted some requests worked intermittently which is what we see. Please escalate — they're considering pausing traffic.

ingrid: assigning action items:
- jon: invalidate edge allowlist for customer 4321 and confirm when done (priority P1)
- alex: draft a short proxy patch to consult Vault revocation flag on allowlist hits for a canary (target: next 24h)
- eng-sre: add an alert for mismatch between proxy allowlist and backend auth failures (we should detect when proxy forwards but backend 403s for same key)
- support (maria): update customer with a mitigation note and ETA

jon: running HDEL now. will post results.

jon: ran command, returned OK. pushed broadcast invalidate to edge nodes. observing 100% 403s for OLD_KEY now (which is expected). :white_check_mark:

maria: confirmed with customer — after a minute they now see 403 consistently. customer accepted that keys are revoked and will rotate to the new key.

ingrid: filing a short incident follow-up to capture root cause and next steps (will include telemetry checks, patch plan, and an audit of customers with long-lived allowlist TTLs). tagging @oncall for a postmortem if needed. :spiral_notepad:

maria: thanks all — please add the incident link here once created and include the patch PR number when available.

alex: creating PR draft for proxy change (will add tests and perf guard). PR: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/proxy/pulls/2345 (WIP)

ingrid: noted. closing this Slack thread once incident doc is up. Thanks :thumbsup:
